info.title: ThreatBridge
info.description: The HTTP API of ThreatBridge's map. docs/API.md has the conventions (times, windows, the time range, filters, queries as POST, writes, errors), the filter grammar and what marks mean. Every response here lists every field it has.

delete.summary: Unmark a host, with the marked flows it is an end of

post.description: Marking a host again replaces its own mark.

put.description: Any invalid mark is a 400 and nothing changes. The map does it to share an opened map's marks, after asking.

post.description: Marking it again replaces its note.

get.summary: One hop: who connected to a host before the anchor, or who it connected to after
get.description: Who connected to ip in the window before the anchor (in), or who it connected to in the window after it (out). Hosts on the exclude list are left out. When the window and the time range don't overlap, start is after end and peers is empty. With filters, counts, times, ports and protocols are those of the flows that pass.

parameters.name: ip
parameters.description: the host

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: in (the default): who connected to it before the anchor; out: who it connected to after

parameters.name: ts
parameters.description: the anchor; blank: now

parameters.name: window
parameters.description: per hop: a number and a unit (s, m, h, d, w), at most max_window; default default_window

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: peers to return, 1 to max_limit (larger values are capped); default default_limit

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: top (most connections, the default) or bottom (rarest)

parameters.name: range_from
parameters.description: the start of the analyst's time range: only flows that started in it count

parameters.name: range_to
parameters.description: the end of the analyst's time range

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: a filter expression (D17); repeat for several, combined with AND

post.summary: One hop: who connected to a host before the anchor, or who it connected to after
post.description: Who connected to ip in the window before the anchor (in), or who it connected to in the window after it (out). Hosts on the exclude list are left out. When the window and the time range don't overlap, start is after end and peers is empty. With filters, counts, times, ports and protocols are those of the flows that pass.

get.summary: Every time-respecting path between two hosts, or between the marked hosts (case backend)
get.description: With src and dst: every path from src to dst, up to limits.paths. With neither: the paths between each pair of marked hosts, each reached when GET /api/compromised says (in a POST, those of its marks), the first limits.paths_per_pair per pair.

parameters.name: src
parameters.description: from this host; with neither src nor dst, the paths between the marked hosts

parameters.name: dst
parameters.description: to this host

parameters.name: src_time
parameters.description: src's IOC time: the first hop leaves src within the window after it

parameters.name: dst_time
parameters.description: dst's IOC time: the path reaches dst by then

parameters.name: window
parameters.description: per hop: a number and a unit (s, m, h, d, w), at most max_window; default default_window

parameters.name: hops
parameters.description: the hop limit, 1 to limits.hops; default threat_hops

parameters.name: range_from
parameters.description: the start of the analyst's time range: only flows that started in it count

parameters.name: range_to
parameters.description: the end of the analyst's time range

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: a filter expression (D17); repeat for several, combined with AND

post.summary: Every time-respecting path between two hosts, or between the marked hosts (case backend)
post.description: With src and dst: every path from src to dst, up to limits.paths. With neither: the paths between each pair of marked hosts, each reached when GET /api/compromised says (in a POST, those of its marks), the first limits.paths_per_pair per pair.

get.summary: A Security Onion Dashboards query and link
get.description: With b: every conversation between a and b, either direction, up to until; without: everything to or from a. The time clause is left out with TB_PIVOT_TIME_CLAUSE=false.

parameters.name: a

parameters.name: b
parameters.description: the other host: every conversation between the two, either direction

parameters.name: until

parameters.name: range_from
parameters.description: the start of the analyst's time range: only flows that started in it count

parameters.name: range_to

parameters.name: range_to
parameters.description: the end of the analyst's time range

post.summary: The marked hosts, and the marked and suspect flows on the drawn connections
post.description: For a CSV export. Without the case backend, the marked flows only.

post.summary: A Security Onion flow's packets, from its sensor through SOC
post.description: The PCAP file, as an attachment, extracted by the sensor that saw the flow, through SOC's Connect API. Needs a SOC API client (TB_SOC_CLIENT_ID, TB_SOC_CLIENT_SECRET; Security Onion Pro), else 501. The request waits for the sensor, up to TB_PCAP_TIMEOUT seconds; a 502 says why the sensor could not provide it, with the SOC job's link where there is one.

mutualTLS.description: a client certificate signed by the ThreatBridge CA (python -m threatbridge serves plain HTTP locally)

write.name: X-ThreatBridge
write.description: required on every write: browsers can't add it to a cross-site request

E400.description: a parameter or the body is invalid; the message says which

E403.description: a write without the X-ThreatBridge header

E409.description: a map is already saved under that name

E500.description: a shared file (exclude list, marks, saved map) is not valid JSON; it is left for someone to fix

E501.description: this needs another backend (threat lines, paths and suspect connections: the case backend; PCAP downloads: Security Onion with a SOC API client)

E502.description: Elasticsearch or SOC failed or answered unexpectedly

pairs.description: each pair of marked hosts with a path between them

start.description: the first flow's start; null for an empty case

end.description: the last flow's start; null for an empty case

dns_names.description: names in the evidence's DNS answers

Config.description: What a client needs to know about this server (D20).

api_version.description: the API version this server speaks

default_window.description: a query's window when it gives none (TB_WINDOW)

default_limit.description: peers per expansion when a query gives none (TB_LIMIT)

max_limit.description: the most peers per expansion (TB_MAX_LIMIT); larger limits are capped

rare_scan_cap.description: distinct peers the rarest scan looks at (TB_RARE_SCAN_CAP)

soc_pivots.description: whether SOC pivots and PCAP links apply (not for the case backend)

analysis.description: whether threat lines and paths are available (case backend)

suspects.description: whether marks hide what isn't on a line through them (POST /api/suspect; case backend)

marks_poll.description: seconds between the map's checks for other analysts' marks

protocol_names.description: how the map names each protocol: {"ssl": "TLS", "krb": "Kerberos", ...}; others in capitals

live_dns.description: whether domain names on the exclude list are also looked up (TB_LIVE_DNS)

case.description: the case backend's evidence; otherwise null

Edge.description: One connection, as the map draws it.

protocols.description: every protocol the flows carry, sorted: named as Zeek names its services (`dns`, `http`, `smb`, `ssl` for TLS, ...), plus `icmp`, and `unknown` for flows nothing identified. Security Onion gives Zeek's own; case files are identified from the payload, then by well-known port

MapDocument.description:
A saved map (D19, D22): its hosts where they were, its connections with their counts as drawn,
the highlights (classes), the view, the toolbar, the filters, its own marks and the queries it was
built from, in order. The map reads only what it understands and leaves out what is malformed.

version.description: 1: saved before filters and marks; it has no filters, marks or queries

settings.description: the toolbar and the paths form: each field's text, by its element id

queries.description: in order, to run again with other filters

classes.description: the highlights (up, down, line-selected, faded, attack, route), and other classes, which opening a map ignores

MapQuery.description: A query the map was built from, with the fields that query took.

op.description: node and edge: a version 1 map's hosts and connections, as converted

map.description: up to limits.map_bytes, kept as it is; the map saves a MapDocument

overwrite.description: replace a map saved under that name; otherwise that is a 409

time.description: when it was reached: the earliest known of its own mark's time and its marked flows' starts; null: unknown

count.description: its own mark, plus the marked flows it is an end of

MarkedQuery.description: The connections drawn, and the query's other parameters (text or numbers).

Marks.description: Marks to use instead of the shared ones (an opened map's own, D19).

MarksView.description: The marks (D15), shared by every analyst.

hosts.description: every marked host, those marked through a marked flow too, sorted by time, unknown first

start.description: the window's start; after end when the window and the time range don't overlap

truncated.description: the rarest scan stopped at rare_scan_cap distinct peers, so the bottom list may be incomplete

status.description: unaffected: no marked host is in its part of the map (hosts joined by the connections sent); hidden: in a part with marks, it carries no marked or suspect flow

Path.description: One chain of flows that proves the path.
